why: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

title: PAC-3 Edge Will Be The Most Capable Patriot Interceptor Ever
body: The new interceptor will sit at the top of the Patriot missile family and promises more range, altitude, and maneuverability against rapidly-developing threats. The post PAC-3 Edge Will Be The Most Capable Patriot Interceptor Ever appeared first on TWZ .
why: Missile defense is one of the biggest budget lines this decade, and its software and sensors are open to newcomers.

title: European U740 Variant Of The XQ-58A Valkyrie Has Flown
body: A team-up of Airbus and Kratos has put the U740 into the sky as Germany races to field advanced air combat drones by 2029. The post European U740 Variant Of The XQ-58A Valkyrie Has Flown appeared first on TWZ .
why: Allies' wars and budgets are the testing ground and a big second market for new defense tech.

title: This Is Our First Look At The Wolf Armored Fighting Vehicle That Aims To Replace The Bradley
body: Wolf is competing against a variant of the German-designed Lynx to become the Army's XM30 Mechanized Infantry Combat Vehicle. The post This Is Our First Look At The Wolf Armored Fighting Vehicle That Aims To Replace The Bradley appeared first on TWZ .
why: Ground robots are moving from demos to real orders, starting with logistics and dangerous jobs.

title: New Coyote Anti-Drone Interceptor Swaps Jet Engine For Rocket Power
body: The Coyote Block 2 is already combat proven, but more capable kamikaze drones have driven a need to fly faster and farther. The post New Coyote Anti-Drone Interceptor Swaps Jet Engine For Rocket Power appeared first on TWZ .
why: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

title: Test Plans Change, Small Distinctions Emerge Between XM30 Bradley Replacement Prototypes
body: Aberdeen Proving Ground and Fort Hood now have the prototype mechanized infantry combat vehicles on hand. The post Test Plans Change, Small Distinctions Emerge Between XM30 Bradley Replacement Prototypes appeared first on TWZ .
why: Ground robots are moving from demos to real orders, starting with logistics and dangerous jobs.

title: U.K. Royal Navy Destroyer Returns Home From Middle East, Strait of Hormuz Multinational Mission in Limbo
body: Royal Navy (RN) destroyer HMS Dragon (D35) returned home to Portsmouth on Friday following a seven-month deployment to the Mediterranean and Middle East.
why: The Navy is short of ships and is turning to cheaper unmanned boats, which opens the door to new builders.

title: Jena-Optronik is proud to partner with MDA Space for its first ASTRO HP mission.
body: MDA Space, a global leader in communications satellites, Earth and space observation, space exploration and infrastructure, will utilize Jena-Optronik’s ASTRO HP star sensor on a LEO mission.
why: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

title: Army awards Defense Unicorns up to $350M for its air-gapped Unified Defense Stack
body: An indefinite-delivery contract for software that ships and runs applications on disconnected, classified and edge networks.
why: Getting software onto air-gapped networks is a bottleneck for every AI vendor. The company that controls deployment becomes infrastructure.

title: DARPA moves four more quantum computing companies into Stage C of its benchmarking initiative
body: That brings the Stage C group to six, the stage where independent evaluators judge whether utility-scale machines can be built.
why: A government-validated quantum shortlist shapes which firms get national-security work.

title: Navy awards Ursa Major $137M for solid rocket motors on two missile programs
body: Part of the push to add domestic second sources for missile propulsion.
why: Rocket motors are the munitions bottleneck. Startups are breaking the two-supplier duopoly.

title: Overland AI gets $4.5M more to field autonomous vehicles with the 75th Ranger Regiment
body: Its total under the APFIT program is now $24.5M.
why: Elite units are the first users of ground autonomy. That is how programs of record start.

title: Goldman upgrades Palantir to Buy ($230 target); Karp says an exec told him to stop hyping Foundry
body: PLTR rose 3.2% while the market fell. Barclays started coverage at Overweight.
why: Commercial AI momentum is now holding up the defense software leader's valuation.

title: Anduril and Navy announce the $6.6B Arsenal-2 submarine-component shipyard in Maryland
body: Anduril invests $3.7B in a 2M sq ft yard at Sparrows Point. A Navy contract worth up to $2.9B, paid per unit produced, covers Virginia-class parts such as torpedo tubes and doors. Operations start in 2030, with 3,100 direct jobs.
why: A venture-backed company is entering heavy shipbuilding, the primes' most protected territory.

title: US Air Force and Australia flight-test the Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile
body: A joint flight test under the US–Australia hypersonics partnership.
why: Hypersonics move toward fielding. Allied co-development (AUKUS) is now the norm.

title: Navy adds $150M of export-ready engineering to Shield AI's X-BAT before its first flight
body: Money to design the aircraft for foreign sales from the start.
why: Autonomous jets are being designed for allied markets from day one. Exports are a growth path.

title: China's 10 Nov magnet deadline collides with DoD's 1 Jan 2027 ban on Chinese magnets
body: Defense suppliers face a squeeze: Beijing is tightening export licensing while the Pentagon bars rare-earth magnets from adversary nations starting 1 January.
why: Every motor, actuator and seeker depends on these magnets. Supply gaps hit drones and munitions first.

title: FY27 opens on a stopgap: the Pentagon is funded at FY26 levels until 11 Dec
body: The continuing resolution passed the Senate 90–6 and the House 370–48. New starts, including DAWG's huge increase, wait for full-year appropriations.
why: Programs that depend on new FY27 money (DAWG, Golden Dome growth) slip until Congress acts.

title: Project Meridian: Musk, Luckey and Gingrich lead a 120-day Pentagon study of future warfare
body: Under CTO Emil Michael, with MITRE managing conflicts of interest. Scope covers AI, robotics, autonomous weapons, directed energy and biotech, from underground to cislunar space. The report is due late January 2027.
why: The founders of the biggest new defense companies are helping set requirements. Read the report when it lands.

title: Epirus Leonidas is the only microwave weapon in DoD's pilot to defend US installations
body: It is also wired into the Army's layered counter-drone network.
why: Defending US bases against drones is now a funded mission.

title: Palantir partners with Armada on sovereign AI infrastructure
body: Palantir software on rugged edge data centers that the customer owns.
why: The software leader is moving into deployable compute for countries that need AI inside their own borders.

title: Hegseth orders a four-star Autonomous Warfare Command and an interim team, Project Agincourt
body: The command would have service-like powers, its own budget and new career fields, with a target of Oct 2027. Agincourt will prototype 'warfighting acquisition'. Congress must act; the SASC bill proposes a robotics combatant command.
why: Drones get a dedicated buyer with its own money: the main future customer for autonomy firms.

title: Anduril and Voyager partner on advanced weapons and propulsion
body: Development, test, qualification and high-rate production for weapons and missile defense.
why: Propulsion is a munitions chokepoint. New entrants are securing supply.

title: Ukrainian troops ordered 590,000+ drones on the Brave1 Market in nine months
body: Ukraine expects about 4.5M FPV drones in 2026 from about 500 makers, with capacity for 8–10M.
why: The volume benchmark that everyone else's drone programs are measured against.

title: Tekever raises $580M at a $6.4B valuation
body: The Portuguese ISR-drone maker's Series D was led by UC Investments and Baillie Gifford.
why: Europe's drone tier is reaching decacorn scale.

title: Northrop and True Anomaly win GHOST-R satellites to inspect objects in geostationary orbit
body: Space Systems Command and DIU prototypes for high-resolution reconnaissance of other satellites.
why: Space control is becoming a budget line, and a startup is sharing it with a prime.

title: Army awards Palantir and Anduril $192M to produce TITAN
body: TITAN, the next-generation mobile intelligence ground station, moves into production.
why: The two new leaders win more as a team than as rivals.

title: Fury officially designated FQ-44A; unit cost said to be well below $20M
body: The Air Force aims for 500 combat-ready CCAs by 2032.
why: A startup-built combat jet at roughly a fifth of a fighter's cost.

title: Army makes its first EW production awards: Heaviside $99M and Research Innovations $96.9M
body: MOTH spectrum analyzers and AI-driven Dragonfly sensors, under a rapid call for solutions.
why: Shows how fast commercial-style contracting can move startups from call to production.

title: Overland AI wins $20M for autonomous minefield breaching
body: One of four companies (with Caterpillar, Forterra and IDV) in the Army's Engineer Autonomous Breaching Capability.
why: Dangerous, repetitive jobs are where ground autonomy gets bought first.

title: Boeing and Anduril downselected for the IFPC Inc 2 second interceptor
body: Both advance in the Army's competition for a cruise-missile and drone defense interceptor.
why: A new entrant competes head-to-head with a prime for interceptor money.

title: AeroVironment wins $464.8M for the first-ever US production contract for a high-energy laser
body: Dozens of 30kW LOCUST X3 lasers for the Army's Enduring-High Energy Laser program, mounted on JLTVs or pallets. Under $5 per shot against Group 1–3 drones.
why: Lasers have moved from demonstrations to production, changing the cost of defending against drones.

title: Navy starts its search for carrier-based CCA Increment 1
body: NAVAIR wants two autonomous prototypes flying within 24 months and certified for shore-based carrier operations within three years.
why: A second large CCA buyer is coming, open to new entrants.

title: Army picks five firms for $2.2B on-base microreactor program (Janus)
body: Antares (Fort Bragg), BWXT (Fort Campbell), GA-EMS (Fort Hood), Radiant (Fort Benning) and Westinghouse (Fort Drum).
why: Bases need resilient power for AI, sensors and lasers. Nuclear startups now have a defense customer.

title: First White House 'Drone Dominance' meeting with about 100 companies
body: The $1.1B program aims for 200,000+ small lethal drones by 2027 through four production 'gauntlets'. Phase one: 12 vendors and 30,000 one-way attack drones at about $5k each, falling toward $2.3k.
why: The government is setting the price for mass-produced drones.

title: Ursa Major to go public in a $2.3B deal
body: The hypersonics and solid-rocket-motor maker is listing.
why: Exits for hard-tech defense companies are reopening.

title: Army awards six prototype contracts for Infantry Last Tactical Mile ground robots
body: Unmanned vehicles for logistics and casualty evacuation; Overland AI and Forterra are among the six.
why: The ground-robot market is forming around logistics first, as it did in Ukraine.

title: Taiwan passes a NT$240B ($7.6B) six-year act for drones and uncrewed systems
body: Taiwan plans 200,000+ UAVs and 1,000 USVs from domestic, non-Chinese supply chains, and has reclassified drones as consumables.
why: A large new buyer of drones and parts free of Chinese supply chains, including from US and Japanese partners.

title: Guetlein: Golden Dome is in jeopardy because of FY27 funding uncertainty
body: The program manager warns that stopgap funding threatens the schedule.
why: Even the top priority depends on appropriations. Don't count on money that hasn't been appropriated.

title: Marines order Epirus's vehicle-mounted microwave weapon
body: A counter-swarm microwave system on vehicles, the successor to ExDECS.
why: Directed energy has moved from demos to orders.

title: Israel's Iron Beam laser still not fully operational eight months after delivery
body: It was tested with Iron Dome in June, drawing on lessons from the 2026 Iran war. The force reportedly wants more than a dozen batteries.
why: Lasers work, but fielding at scale is slow. There is an opening for power, cooling and integration suppliers.

title: Hadrian raises $1.37B at $7.87B for automated factories
body: Anchored by JPMorgan's strategic fund, with Valor, Baillie Gifford, Founders Fund, a16z and 1789 Capital.
why: Factory automation for the supply base is now a venture category, not just a cost center.

title: Blue Water Autonomy wins a spot on the Navy's $40M deep-ocean mapping contract
body: Long-endurance autonomous ships to survey the Indian and Pacific oceans.
why: Survey work is an early way for autonomous-ship makers to earn revenue while combat programs are contested.

title: Palantir Q2'26: revenue +93% to $1.935B; US commercial +149%
body: US government $809M (+90%), US commercial $764M (+149%), Rule of 40 score 155. FY26 guidance raised to $8.150–8.158B.
why: Commercial revenue is about to overtake US government revenue, which spreads the defense leader's risk.

title: Air Force could choose up to six vendors for CCA Increment 2
body: Nine vendors are in concept refinement and a pool of 20+ may compete. The Air Force is revisiting production goals 'with an eye on scale'.
why: The second round of the biggest autonomous aircraft program is still open.

title: Primes post record backlogs: Lockheed $230B, RTX $289B; guidance raised
body: Lockheed's Q2 sales rose 11% to $20.1B, Missiles & Fire Control +19% (PAC-3, THAAD, PrSM), helped by a $35B THAAD multiyear. Northrop also hit a record.
why: Missile defense and munitions are a boom for incumbents too. New entrants are adding to the market, not replacing them.

title: Karman Space & Defense buys Walker Precision Engineering ($93M), its largest deal yet
body: Karman, up ~200% since its IPO, keeps rolling up niche suppliers. It also agreed to buy Seemann Composites and MSC for $220M.
why: Public newcomers are consolidating the supplier base, a path to exit for component startups.

title: Neros wins a $500M Army IDIQ for Archer FPV drones
body: Under the Purpose Built Attritable Systems program. Output reached about 1,200 drones a week by August.
why: FPV drones are a program of record; the Ukraine model has become US doctrine.

title: Blue Water Autonomy and Saildrone sue the Navy over the MUSV rejection
body: A protest over the Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel selection.
why: New entrants are using the courts against legacy-style procurement. Expect more.

title: Helsing raises at about an $18B valuation
body: Reports put the round at $1.2–1.8B. Its HX-2 strike drone is in Ukrainian service, alongside a €1.46B drone contract.
why: Europe's answer to Palantir plus Anduril is now a top-three private defense company.

title: Quantum Systems signs a €1B Series D at about €7B
body: Co-led by Blackstone, Noteus, Airbus and Advent.
why: Airbus investing signals European incumbents are buying into drone makers.

title: China adds MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export-control list
body: Effective immediately, Chinese exports of dual-use items to both companies are banned.
why: Beijing is targeting the US effort to build its own rare-earth supply chain. Heavy rare earths are the pressure point.

title: AUKUS partners test drone-swarming tactics
body: Australian, US and UK soldiers trialled swarms under AUKUS Pillar II.
why: Allied autonomy standards are forming. Firms that can interoperate across the three nations gain.

title: Japan launches a Rapid Interceptor Drone Acquisition Program modelled on Ukraine
body: Systems are to be selected for trials within about three months.
why: Interceptor drones are going global. Asian buyers are open to foreign vendors.

title: CSIS: 'Why software, not drones, will decide the next war'
body: After a 5 June presidential memorandum on autonomy, CSIS argues that AI kill chains, the software that fuses sensors, picks targets and times strikes, are themselves autonomous weapons.
why: Policy definitions will decide who must certify what. That is a compliance market and a moat.

title: Air Force orders CCA production from General Atomics and Anduril
body: The first combat jet built by a defense startup goes into production.
why: Proves the build-before-the-contract model on the hardest product category.

title: SpaceX wins $6.45B across two Golden Dome and space-communications awards
body: $4.16B for SB-AMTI (tracking moving air targets from space) and $2.29B for the Space Data Network backbone, built on MILNET/Starshield, with an operational prototype due by end-2027.
why: One company now holds the military's space backbone, a concentration risk and a platform others will build on.

title: Castelion signs a first-of-its-kind production deal for the Blackbeard hypersonic missile
body: Its Project Ranger site in New Mexico will make at least 500 a year once testing is complete. The company was later valued at about $13B after an $800M raise.
why: Low-cost hypersonics built like consumer hardware challenges the primes' strike franchise.

title: CDAO raises Scale AI's Pentagon deal to $500M
body: Up from $100M in 2025. Covers data labeling and decision support for military AI.
why: The data and evaluation layer under military AI is its own large market.

title: Anduril raises $5B Series H at $61B
body: Its valuation doubled in 11 months. Talks were reported near $100B by July.
why: Private capital can now fund factories, once the primes' moat.

title: Shield AI's Hivemind to run Taiwan's Thunder Tiger sea drones
body: AI autonomy for a coastal-denial network of unmanned surface vessels.
why: US autonomy software combined with allied hardware is a repeatable export model.

title: CBO: Golden Dome could cost $1.2T over 20 years; DoW estimate $185B to 2035
body: Independent estimates range from $175B (White House) to $3.6T (AEI) depending on the design.
why: A huge, contested budget line. Its political survival will shape space and missile-defense startups.

title: FY27 request: $54.6B for DAWG and $53.6B for Drone Dominance
body: DAWG rises from $225M. The drone effort includes $39.2B for autonomous systems procurement and domestic production plus $14.4B for counter-unmanned systems.
why: The biggest budget shift toward autonomy ever. Follow it through Congress.

title: PitchBook: defense-tech VC hits $69.5B over the trailing 12 months
body: Q1 set a record at $19.8B across 262 deals; Q2 brought $16.4B across 249. Autonomy took 42.1% of Q2. Eleven public listings reopened exits.
why: Money concentrates in mega-rounds and seed; mid-stage is hard.

title: Space Force picks 12 firms, including SpaceX, Anduril, Lockheed and True Anomaly, for space-based interceptor prototypes
body: Awards total up to $3.2B, with a demonstration due by 2028.
why: Missile defense, once the primes' preserve, now includes new entrants.

title: Ukraine to field 25,000 ground robots for frontline logistics
body: About 280 companies make 550+ ground-vehicle models, running 10,000+ logistics missions a month.
why: The clearest demand signal yet for ground autonomy, years ahead of the US.

title: DoD components face an 'aggressive' timeline to move onto Maven Smart System
body: Deputy Secretary Feinberg pushed Maven toward a department-wide program of record.
why: How a vendor becomes the standard; once every command runs on Maven, replacing it is very hard.

title: Germany and Ukraine sign a €4B package that includes joint drone production
body: Part of Europe's push to scale autonomous-systems manufacturing.
why: Ukrainian know-how plus European money is becoming a production base that will compete with US firms.

title: Saronic raises $1.75B Series D at $9.25B
body: For autonomous surface vessels and shipyard capacity.
why: Naval autonomy is the next large hardware market.

title: RAND: crosscutting insights for the drone-dominance push
body: Large numbers of attritable, adaptable unmanned systems now cost orders of magnitude less than traditional platforms.
why: Research support for the cheap-mass thesis.

title: Shield AI raises $1.5B Series G at $12.7B
body: Led by Advent and co-led by JPMorgan; Blackstone added $500M of preferred equity.
why: AI pilot software is valued as its own layer, separate from airframes.

title: Anduril and Palantir reported to be leading Golden Dome's software layer
body: Teamed with SpaceX for parts of the constellation; they lead the software that links sensors to interceptors.
why: The command core of the decade's largest program went to newcomers.

title: PLA demonstrates the 'Atlas' swarm: one vehicle launches 96 drones; claims of 200 per operator
body: The drones fly an autonomous anti-jamming path-planning algorithm tested under electromagnetic interference.
why: The pacing threat for US swarm and counter-swarm programs. It drives requirements.

title: Drone Dominance Gauntlet I: 25 vendors compete, 11 selected
body: Held at Fort Benning. About 100 operators flew each system after two hours of training.
why: Easy to learn and cheap to buy beat exotic performance.

title: First known microwave kill of a jam-proof fiber-optic drone
body: Epirus Leonidas disabled a fiber-optic-guided drone in a live-fire demo.
why: Fiber-optic drones made jamming obsolete in parts of Ukraine; microwave weapons and interceptors are the answer.

title: Hanwha Defense USA and HavocAI agree to co-develop 200-ft autonomous surface vessels
body: Korean shipbuilding paired with US collaborative-autonomy software. HavocAI later advanced to Navy MUSV at-sea testing.
why: Foreign shipyards plus US autonomy could relieve the Navy's capacity crunch.
